# bilibili-drum-score-to-pdf

One repository, two independent products for turning visible vertical drum score videos into A4 PDFs. The root README is the shared entry point.

The self-contained Agent Skill lives in skills/bilibili-drum-score-to-pdf/. Install that whole directory, including scripts, references and LICENSE. It uses its own pinned requirements and Agent image/page review protocol. The default route preserves continuous score images; explicit requests enable optional redraw or vector workflows. It does not import or call the website.

The standalone Python/CLI and optional FastAPI website live in src/drum_score/. Install with pyproject.toml in a separate Python 3.12+ environment; the web extra adds service dependencies. The public website is https://drum.kenqia.top/. It uses BBDownNext 2.3.0 metadata-bounded.1 with direct egress, never loads Skill protocols, and has no model generation or Agent approval step. Complete means artifact publication, with reliable=false. Web results expire after 24 hours.

Both need native FFmpeg/ffprobe/Poppler. The website service lifecycle is Ubuntu/Linux-specific. Anonymous acquisition must not load user cookies or credentials. Keep task state, dependencies and output directories separate; existing output is never overwritten.

Run tests/skill and root tests in separate Python processes; their fixtures and module names overlap. Synthetic assertions do not prove actual Agent image review, source approval, model calls or musical proofreading. Historical evidence stays in docs/experiments and Git; restoring the Skill does not resolve old source uncertainties.

Code and documentation use MIT. Music, notation and derived examples retain their owners' rights. See LICENSE and docs/media/readme/README.md.
